cohort: 250 women presenting to participating rural hospitals in Queensland, Australia, with an estimated due date in 2016
finding: A high prevalence of obesity was found in the rural obstetric population, and increasing BMI was associated with increased birth weight, gestational diabetes, transfer rate, and cesarean section rate.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal body mass index was associated with an increased likelihood of transfer to a larger birthing center, diagnosis of gestational diabetes, and both elective and emergency cesarean sections.
